verdict.reasoning: Patient describes 'it's diarrhea... super watery' and timing: 'it's been about three days now.'
Frequency: 'I feel like it's like almost every hour I'm awake.' Consistency and no blood: 'it's just super watery... Have you noticed any blood in your stools?... No... there's nothing like that.'

Pain description: 'I feel a cramp and then I know it's time to go.' Location: 'it's like at the bottom... it feels pretty like in the middle to me.' Severity: patient estimates 'maybe is that like a six or seven?'
Nausea: 'Yeah, I definitely feel kind of nauseous.'
Vomiting after milk: 'whenever I have, like, milk... I just feel like I want to vomit. And actually, yeah, one time I just, like, had some milk and I just completely vomited it.'
Subjective fever: 'I think I am pretty. I feel kind of really hot all the time, and I. Pretty sure I'm burning up... I haven't actually done any temperature reading.'
Fluids passing through: 'I'm trying to drink a lot of water... it just feels like it's going straight through. Just feels like it's going straight through.'
Urine frequency: 'Are you passing urine? Okay.' Patient: 'Yeah, but I guess less frequently maybe, but it seems to be okay.'

No past medical history: 'are you otherwise fit and well or do you have any other medical history?' Patient: 'Yeah, I think otherwise I'm fit. Well... I can't think of any related medical history... no, I don't think so.'
Paracetamol use: 'I haven't been, I'm not on any regular medication... I've been taking some, like, paracetamols and stuff like that lately.'
No allergies: 'And do you have any allergies to any medications?' Patient: 'So I don't have any allergies that I know of.'
Father’s cancer: 'My dad actually has colon cancer at the moment... he's sort of in his third stage.' (Stage III colon cancer.)
Living situation: 'I live with my um, sister and my mum.'
Brother’s similar illness: 'my brother has had, actually had something like this... he has it as well, for five days as well.'
Work: 'I work at an office in central London. It's. So I work in government.'
Smoking: 'So I smoke, I smoke for like socially but not like regularly. So normally if it's a Friday... I might have a cigarette.'

Alcohol: 'I might have a beer during the weekdays... Maybe on Fridays I have more alcohol... not every week but maybe once or twice a month that... I'll go out with my friends and we'll drink a lot.' (Social use with monthly binge episodes.)
Assessment: 'your symptoms are suggestive of something called gastroenteritis. A bit of a basic infection of your tummy.' This is in context of 3 days of acute watery diarrhea.

Nausea/vomiting with milk: patient notes 'I definitely feel kind of nauseous... whenever I have, like, milk... I just feel like I want to vomit... one time... had some milk and I just completely vomited it.'

Risk of dehydration is implied by 'You're losing a lot of fluid there' and later: 'if you are getting dehydrated, then we need to do further investigations.' High stool frequency and decreased urine output were documented earlier.
Family history: 'My dad actually has colon cancer at the moment... he's sort of in his third stage.' Doctor: 'I'll make a note of that because it's always important to know these kind of details.'

ORS and fluids: 'you can get things like diurelite, which is a fluid replacement we can get from the pharmacy... You can just get over the counter.' and 'Make sure. You drink plenty of fluids.' plus emphasis on keeping 'well hydrated.'

Diet and avoid alcohol: 'clear fluids you can use soft diet, things like soup, mash, and then gradually build up as much as your body can tolerate. But really, let's try and keep yourself well hydrated first.' and 'Try and avoid alcohol if you can.'

Paracetamol recommendation: 'You can try just, you know, regular paracetamol if you are feeling feverish.' and later: 'If you've got bit of tummy pain, if you're feeling feverish, then I think paracetamol is very sensible.'
No other meds: Only diurelite (an OTC ORS) and paracetamol are suggested; no prescriptions or additional medications are ordered in the transcript.
Antibiotics are never mentioned or prescribed during the consult, so stating none were initiated is consistent with the transcript.

Follow-up: 'if your symptoms aren't settling down in the next couple of days, so 48 hours, I want you to give me a call back because... if you are getting dehydrated, then we need to do further investigations.' This implies reassessment and possible in-person evaluation.
Visit type: starts as 'It's audio. No, no, it's absolutely fine.' There are no vitals or physical examination findings documented anywhere in the transcript.
